newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Consortia aim for Brazilian control of CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Consortia aim for Brazilian control of CVRD.

text.p: The two consortia battling to win a strategic stake in Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce SA (CVRD) plan to keep control of the company in Brazilian hands even though foreign investors are footing much of the bill.

Brazil's largest conglomerate, the family-run Votorantim group with interests in the cement, metals, paper and pulp sectors, which put together the Valecom consortium, plans to play a significant role in the privatized company.

Should Valecom win the April 29 auction of a 40-45-percent voting stake in CVRD, then Votorantim Chief Executive Antonio Ermirio de Moraes will be made chairman of the special purpose company administering the strategic stake.
"For us it was a fundamental issue to keep the center of decision making on CVRD in Brazil," Moraes said in an interview with Jornal do Brasil.

Otherwise, Votorantim will be running Valecom together with its main partner, South African mining group Anglo American Corp. Both companies have equal stakes in the consortium amounting to more than 50 percent jointly.

Valepar, the other consortium bidding for CVRD, has a less autocratic view of how the strategic stake in CVRD should be administered with plans to balance and share power between its constituting members, while ensuring the predominance of Brazilian investors.

"Given the importance CVRD represents for Brazil...we thought that the capital (of Valepar) had to be predominantly Brazilian," said Benjamin Steinbruch, chairman of Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN, which is leading Valepar.
Valepar's member companies will each be limited to a maximum 20-25 percent stake in the consortium.
Should Valepar win the auction, it would also create a fund, the "Fundo Brasil", that would allow ordinary Brazilians and small and medium size companies to acquire a stake in Valepar.

Apart from CSN, which was itself privatized only four years ago, the other Brazilian members of Valepar are paper and pulp firm Cia. Suzano Companhia Suzano de Papel e Celulose, a group of four pension funds and Opportunity Asset Managment, an offshore investment fund for foreign, mainly U.S., investors.
Bradesco, Brazil's largest retail bank, will act as a financing agent to one or more of Valepar's members.
Suzano is Brazil's leading cardboard producer and also has interests in the petrochemical sector.

The four pension funds include Banco do Brasil's pension fund, Previ -- Brazil's largest with a net worth of 17.4 billion reais ($16.4 billion) -- as well as Petros, the pension fund for state oil monopoly Petrobras ; Funcef, the Caixa Economica fund; and Funcesp, the pension fund of state power firm Cesp.
Valepar's foreign stakeholders are Nations Bank and U.S. aluminium firm Alcoa.
Foreign investors are more strongly represented in Valecom, which includes a group of 11 Japanese steelmakers and trading companies led by Nippon Steel Corp with a joint 10 percent stake.
Japan's Mitsui & Co Ltd is also represented via Brazil's metal and metallurgical group Caemi in which it recently acquired a 40 percent stake.
Valecom's only other Brazilian members are two pension funds, the Central Bank fund, Centrus, and telecoms giant Telebras fund Sistel.
